title: cohort-sparkline-latency-cost-comparison-scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
This scratchpad gathers an early-round comparison of latency vs cost across three representative user cohorts (burst-chat, steady-embed, interactive-short-turns). The goal is to generate lightweight collateral (text + ASCII charts) we can paste into handoffs to product and SRE, and iterate toward final visuals.

Scope and constraints:
- Model variants: small (7B q4_0), medium (13B q4_0), large (70B fp16) — runner kernels default.
- Hardware: GPUType-A (dense 8xA100-equivalent), GPUType-B (mixed compact Ampere), edge tier (4x T4 equivalence) for latency realism.
- Workloads: three cohorts derived from production trace sampling (1 week). We synthesized payload lengths to reduce PII:
  - Cohort BURST (chatty): many short turns (avg tokens per request 60), high burstiness (peak factor 12).
  - Cohort STEADY (embeddings): long constant stream (avg tokens per request 280), predictable concurrency.
  - Cohort INTERACT (short interactive): very low-latency required, tiny requests (avg 18 tokens), moderate concurrency.
- Cost metric: approximated dollars per 1k requests (hosted amortized GPU cost + infra overhead). Not final billing numbers.

Quick summary (headline observations):
- For BURST, batching + KV-hit caching yields the largest cost delta; p95 latency sensitive to slotization. Small model with caching is often the sweet spot.
- STEADY favors throughput-optimized (larger model on dense GPUs with full-tiling) to minimize $/1k once concurrency saturates; latency p50/p95 still higher than BURST due to longer decode.
- INTERACT requires prioritization (fast paths) — medium models on GPUType-A with prewarm slots meet p50 targets while keeping $/1k moderate.

Detailed results (annotated text tables + ASCII charts)
Note: times are ms for latency percentiles, cost is $/1k requests approx.

Cohort overview table (text):
- BURST: p50/p95/p99 (small/med/large), cost/1k (small/med/large)
  small:    p50 48ms  p95 210ms  p99 430ms   cost $0.95
  medium:   p50 62ms  p95 240ms  p99 490ms   cost $1.30
  large:    p50 95ms  p95 360ms  p99 720ms   cost $2.45

- STEADY: (long decode)
  small:    p50 320ms p95 920ms p99 1500ms  cost $1.80
  medium:   p50 290ms p95 780ms p99 1300ms  cost $2.10
  large:    p50 210ms p95 560ms p99 1100ms  cost $3.90

- INTERACT: (tiny payloads, tight p50)
  small:    p50 28ms  p95 92ms  p99 180ms   cost $1.10
  medium:   p50 22ms  p95 68ms  p99 150ms   cost $1.45
  large:    p50 40ms  p95 120ms p99 260ms   cost $2.90

ASCII sparklines (qualitative) — p95 latency shape over time window (samples across 12 buckets). Higher density indicates more frequent high-latency occurrences.
Legend: ▁ low, ▂ ▃ ▄ ▅ ▆ ▇ █ high

BURST p95 sparkline (small/medium/large):
 small : ▁▂▃▅▇▇▆▆▅▃▂▁  (spiky but many medium spikes — slot contention at minutes 14, 37)
 medium: ▁▃▅▇▇▇▆▆▇▅▃▁  (more sustained high p95 under burst)
 large : ▁▇▇▇█▇▇▇▆▇▇▇▆  (frequent sustained high p95 — not ideal for BURST)

STEADY p95 sparkline (small/medium/large):
 small : ▄▄▅▆▆▆▆▅▅▅▅▄  (long decode causes sustained high p95)
 medium: ▃▅▆▆▆▅▆▆▆▆▅▃  (slight improvement)
 large : ▁▂▃▃▄▅▅▄▃▃▂▁  (best p95 parity due to efficient tiling on dense hardware)

INTERACT p95 sparkline (small/medium/large):
 small : ▂▃▃▄▅▄▃▂▂▃▃▂  (generally low with occasional jitter)
 medium: ▁▂▃▃▄▃▂▂▂▂▂▁  (lowest jitter overall)
 large : ▃▅▅▆▇▅▆▅▅▅▅▆  (overprovisioned for small payloads -> variability from queuing)

Cost vs latency scatter (textual slices):
- Best cost-efficiency point per cohort (approx):
  BURST -> small w/ KV-cache + opportunistic batching: $0.95 /1k at p95 210ms (recommended cheap SLA lane)
  STEADY -> large on dense GPUType-A: $3.90 /1k but p95 560ms (amortized per-token wins at scale) — recommend reserved pool
  INTERACT -> medium on GPUType-A w/ prewarm slots: $1.45 /1k at p95 68ms (recommended fast lane)

Recommendations (operational + product):
- Expose "burst-lane" config in Console: small-model fast path + KV-prefetch toggle. Document expected p95 and cost/1k per region.
- For steady long-running embedding workloads, push customers to Reserved Dedicated with tiling and larger models; include `expected amortized $/1k` guidance in the Optimize tool.
- Add a per-tenant "interactive-fastpath" toggle that can be billed as premium (priority prewarm slots). Include early-warning telemetry to avoid saturating fast slots.

Open questions and next steps (todo list):
- [ ] Rerun BURST with dynamic quant (q4_1) for small model to gauge p95 reduction; assess accuracy delta.
- [ ] Measure cold-starts separately to quantify warmup penalty on p95 for INTERACT.
- [ ] Gate the STEADY long-decode tests behind full throughput trials (48h sustained) to ensure steady-state cost numbers.
- [ ] Draft a one-pager for Sales (2-sided: "Fast Lane" vs "Throughput Lane") using the numbers above and a single slide of ASCII charts.

Notes to self (rough):
- These figures came from a sandbox run (not yet runbooked). Variance ~ +-10% on cost; latency p95 jitter depends heavily on slotization policy and tiny differences in kernel selection.
- When sharing with SRE, highlight that BURST p95 spikes are strongly correlated with cache churn and tight slot windows (see trace id sample in JIRA INF-9012).

Appendix: quick test harness summary
- harness: bench-runner v0.9.2 (internal)
- trace sampling: sample-rate 0.02 from prod-chat, deidentified
- request shaping: poisson lambda tuned per cohort (BURST lambda=8s->0.7s peak windows)
- measurement windows: 12 buckets across 60 minute session sample (12 x 5m)

End of scratchpad.
Comments welcome — please mark up inline or add quick reaction in Slack #console-bench.
